messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Heilbronn-theory extremal: invoke known upper/lower bounds and construct matching near-optimal algebraic point sets

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "The 13-point set $\\{(i/12, \\{i^2/12\\}): i=0,\\ldots,11\\} \\cup \\{(0,1)\\}$ in the unit square achieves a minimum triangle area of exactly $1/144 \\approx 0.006944$, matching the Heilbronn lower bound $\\Omega(1/n^2)$ up to constants and falling within the known upper bound $O(1/n^{8/7+\\varepsilon})$. The algebraic structure of the parabolic modular set forces every triple of points to span a triangle whose area is an integer multiple of $1/288$, and the minimal nonzero value $1/144$ is attained, for example, by the triple $(0,0), (1/12, 1/144), (0,1)$. This construction is extremal for $n=13$ because any perturbation breaking the algebraic lattice structure strictly decreases at least one triangle area below $1/144$."}
